233.t: Red Norvo's urgent call about Las Vegas
233.s: Norvo phoned repeatedly about a three-week Las Vegas job, and the very word angered Monk.
233.q: I got a call, because my folks knew where I was at. They said, 'You got a very, very serious call from Red Norvo, and he said it was very urgent.' And I said, 'We don't really

233.s: Tropicana's entertainment director wanted jazz in the lounge; Monk said he'd go only if Red were stuck, and Red said he was.
233.q: He said...Red's a nice man, easy spoken. And he could see that I wasn't happy, I wasn't excited about him calling me. So he proceeded to tell me that this was a good job. The guy that called him was entertainment director of the Tropicana, a friend of his from Los Angeles. He used to own the…

233.t: End of Las Vegas jazz at the Tropicana; the Blue Room acts
233.s: Jazz ended with the Red Norvo Trio while the Blue Room brought in Basie, Sarah Vaughan, Armstrong and others.
233.q: But he forgot to mention, to bear in mind...So things were going great, we thought Maynard would be there forever so automatically we'd be there forever. Why would the guy want to sell the hotel? We never thought about that. It was just ridiculous.

233.s: Monk turned down hotel showroom work, seeing it as tokenism, because it was not playing.
233.q: Somewhat, because what happened after that, I felt like...I was having a problem getting a job. Not just a job. I could have...and I've had some people talk to me strictly private, even a union official: 'Monk, you know you're really liked here. It will be no problem that you can get a job in one…

233.t: Why he started fighting for jazz in Las Vegas
233.s: Unable to find a jazz outlet, Monk turned from performing to hustling, growing angry.
233.q: : Yeah, it is, it was. But it's one of the other things that I say it's funny how some other things that happen to me that had to do with fate. There was a reason for it, I guess.

233.t: The Hilton entertainment director and the four-wall idea
233.s: A liberal Hilton director invited Monk in and suggested four-walling, but died of a heart attack.
233.q: : I was here, and into it again. Really into it. By this time, now, I'm carrying around a little briefcase, trying to talk to this guy, trying to talk to that entertainment director. Can't see this one, trying to talk to somebody that knew that one...

233.t: The M-G-M nostalgia theater jazz proposal
233.s: Monk wrote a proposal for jazz in the M-G-M theater and monthly Sunday spectaculars after Bill DeAngeles asked for it on paper.
233.q: Bill DeAngeles thought it was a great concept, and 'I think so-and-so.' And I sat in his office and talked with him. He said, 'The one thing you have to do is put this on paper. You have to bring me a proposal, so I can submit it to the board. I can't go over there and say, well, Monk's got a great…

233.s: The M-G-M executive said he was not interested and would not discuss it, Monk's biggest disappointment.
233.q: That's a major disappointment. More major than all of them because when the guy said, 'I'm not interested' and didn't even want to talk about it, not even the courtesy of saying that...like, if he can put it another way, even. But after the work I went through, after he's saying that's what they…

233.t: Fighting the system: Billboard and the phone threats
233.s: After telling the trades what he was told, Monk got phone calls telling him to drop the names.
233.q: Well, the jazz society came because, that was like, forced you to go somewhere. You either had to give it up or go into something else. I wasn't near about to give it up. It just made me an angry man and I had to pick up arms toward that. I had to fight the system, if that's what it was. There was…

233.t: Working with The Drifters at the Sahara
233.s: A month in the Sahara lounge with the Drifters was among his worst musical experiences, but got him back to Las Vegas.
233.q: : I got a call from a local musician to come up and work with The Drifters. And I said, 'This guy has got to be kidding.' And he said, 'Well, Monk, it's for a whole month at the Sahara, in the lounge.' He said, now, he's talking and he's working gigs with them, and he'd worked with them when they…

407.t: Feeling held back; the jazz tree and big-band players
407.s: On being held back, he complains jazz is seen as entertainment, and defends Vegas and Chitlin Circuit players.
407.q: Yeah. I feel like that right now, because they got it as entertainment only. You know? Because if you look at that, those trees that they have with the roots of jazz you know, down at the bottom they got Satchmo and Bix Beiderbecke, and then they got, you know, the different people you know. And…
